quotes.text: They must complete authentication within 15 minutes of inactivity; three incorrect one-time password attempts fail authentication.

old_evidence.text: To pay with GrabPay, customers are redirected to GrabPay’s website, where they have to authenticate the transaction using a one-time password.
1Not supported when using Checkout in subscription mode or setup mode.2Express Checkout Element doesn’t support GrabPay.
GrabPay payments can be refunded up to 90 days after the original payment.

findings: The November capture identifies GrabPay as single-use wallet with provisional access, immediate confirmation label, standard payout schedule, MY/SG merchants and customers, MYR/SGD presentment and domestic-only coverage (new raw lines 9-35). The May capture had the country, currency, wallet, redirect, no-recurring and payout facts but lacked the domestic-only and access labels (old raw lines 8-59). Current source lines 13-21 captures the broad route but not the new coverage boundary.

New matrix explicitly supports full/partial refunds and Invoicing, but no recurring, Billing, setup_future_usage, SetupIntents or off-session payments; it supports in-app payments while Express Checkout Element is unsupported (new raw lines 34-58, 81-105). The old product list plus footnote excluded Checkout subscription/setup modes and Express Checkout Element (old raw lines 61-71). Current source line 23 incorrectly says no partial refund is noted despite old raw line 52's Yes/Yes and new raw lines 50-52's explicit support; line 25's 'Subscriptions not listed' should become the explicit no-recurring/Billing/setup boundary, not inference from absence.

New refund text adds a maximum 90-day submission window, no cancellation, never a reversal, return to original GrabPay balance or linked funding source, status via Refund object and refund.updated/refund.failed, and fallback credit obligation if failed (new raw lines 50-73). Old raw lines 96-98 already documented the 90 days, async up-to-five-minute processing and outcome webhooks; source lines 13, 23 omit lifecycle and failure/uncancellable qualifications.

New customer flow says browser/webview OTP authentication must complete within 15 minutes of inactivity, with three bad OTP attempts failing authentication; return via configured return URL, URL scheme or universal link displays the PaymentIntent result (new raw lines 110-122). Old raw lines 8-10 gives only web redirect; source line 19's site-only return is too narrow for documented app paths. Browser return and instant provisional access are not proof of PaymentIntent success.

New transaction identifier rules distinguish merchant/payment descriptor formatting and variable customer display, connected-account direct-charge versus platform-default destination-charge descriptor, and GrabPay transaction ID at latest_charge.payment_method_details.grabpay.transaction_id, distinct from Charge and PaymentIntent IDs (new raw lines 124-130). The current source lines 11-33 lacks this important identity/account boundary.

The raw new pricing URL has an undefined path segment (new raw line 15). It cannot support an amount or fee inference. Current source frontmatter lines 1-9 lacks canonical_url and only lists the old dated raw; a source correction should add https://docs.stripe.com/payments/grabpay and both provenance entries while retaining 2026-05-07 versus 2026-11-07 dates.
substantive_changes: Explicit domestic-only eligibility, single-use/provisional/immediate labels and detailed unsupported capabilities, including no SetupIntents/off-session, refine the older broad property and product lists (old raw lines 12-71; new raw lines 10-58, 81-105).

Refund cancellation, reversal, funding-source and failed-refund details and authentication timeout/OTP attempt limits are newly documented in the November capture (old raw lines 73-102; new raw lines 59-79, 110-122).
The descriptor ownership and true GrabPay transaction-ID path are new material identity facts (new raw lines 124-130; absent old raw lines 1-106).
historical_claims_to_preserve: May 7, 2026 old raw lines 61-71 explicitly excluded Checkout subscription/setup modes and Express Checkout Element; the new raw lines 87, 101-105 still make setup/recurring unsupported. Keep older wording dated rather than infer that its footnote was revoked by omission.

Old raw lines 96-106 retain refund, dispute and GrabPay-branding evidence; new raw lines 59-79, 106-108 restate and expand these. The old demo video at old raw lines 73-76 is navigation/presentation, not behavioral proof or a current asset guarantee.
conflicts: Current source line 23 says partial refund was not noted even though old raw line 52 says Yes/Yes and new raw lines 50-52 explicitly support partial and full refunds; correct this baseline summary error, not a new raw reversal.

Current source line 19 says return to merchant site; new raw lines 118-122 include browser/webview and return to website or app through URL/scheme/universal link. This is a scope expansion, not proof that every platform path has been configured.

Current source line 25 describes subscriptions as merely not listed, while old raw lines 30-32, 71 and new raw lines 35, 93, 103-105 explicitly exclude recurring/Billing/setup/off-session paths; clarify the conditional product matrix.

Current source line 21 says OTP prevents chargebacks; both captures say no standard dispute/chargeback process (old raw lines 100-102; new raw lines 75-79), not that authentication universally prevents fraud, complaints or refunds.
unresolved_questions: Document capture does not verify a particular MY/SG merchant's activation, account permissions, Connect configuration or Stripe/GrabPay payment outcome (new raw lines 18-33, 118-130).
The undefined pricing link at new raw line 15 does not establish current GrabPay fees; no pricing claims should be drawn from it.
Quickstart, sample, manual configuration and branding assets are linked navigation (new raw lines 106-108, 132-138); their contents and current availability were not read in this job.

findings: Add canonical_url https://docs.stripe.com/payments/grabpay and both dated raw file references to frontmatter lines 1-9/Raw Sources lines 31-33.

Correct line 23's partial-refund ambiguity: old raw line 52 and new raw lines 50-52 both support partial and full refunds; add the new cancellation, refund-source, failure and status caveats from new raw lines 59-73.

Expand line 19's return flow for browser/webview and app schemes, 15-minute inactivity and three-bad-OTP failure (new raw lines 110-122), and preserve that return/provisional access is not payment success.
Summarize domestic MY/SG, no setup_future_usage/SetupIntents/off-session/Billing and supported Invoicing/in-app distinctions (new raw lines 18-35, 81-105).
Add descriptor ownership and GrabPay transaction ID versus Stripe IDs (new raw lines 124-130), and scope no-disputes wording to standard chargebacks.
conflicts: Source line 23 contradicts both captures' partial-refund support; line 25 understates explicit no-recurring/setup matrix.
Source line 19 is website-only while new capture allows app return; line 21 implies authentication prevents all chargeback risk beyond the documented no-standard-dispute rule.
source_assessments.reason: Material new eligibility, refund, auth, and transaction-identity facts plus baseline inaccuracies require a dated source update; review-only worker does not edit canonical pages.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/grabpay, GrabPay is a single-use MY/SG domestic wallet presented in MYR/SGD. The customer selects it, authenticates a browser or webview redirect with a one-time password, and returns through a website or app URL to see the PaymentIntent success or failure result; the return itself and provisional access do not prove success. The new capture adds a 15-minute inactivity limit and three wrong-OTP failure condition, no setup/recurring/off-session support, and a distinct GrabPay transaction ID under the latest Charge (new raw lines 9-35, 81-130). The old capture states the basic redirect, country/currency and refund route but lacks those boundaries (old raw lines 8-71, 96-102). source-stripe-grabpay.md summarizes the old route but incorrectly doubts partial refunds, narrows return to a website, and lacks descriptor-account and transaction-ID distinctions (source lines 13-29).
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/grabpay, substantive additions are domestic-only eligibility and explicit no-SetupIntent/off-session capability, uncancellable asynchronous refunds returned to the original funding source, OTP timeout and failure limits, app return options, and descriptor/account/GrabPay transaction-ID boundaries (old raw lines 12-106; new raw lines 16-130). The old video demo and changed quickstart/asset links are presentation or navigation, not live payment proof. Preserve the May 2026 old Checkout subscription/setup exclusion and 90-day refund history, while source-stripe-grabpay.md gains the dated November raw and canonical URL. Warn reciprocally that the source's partial-refund caveat contradicts both raw captures, its site-only return omits app paths, and its 'OTP prevents chargebacks' phrasing exceeds the no-standard-dispute rule. Dashboard enablement, customer browser return, and instant provisional access are not account eligibility, PaymentIntent success, or settled funds. The new raw pricing URL contains undefined and supports no fee inference.
